breaking.headline: Iran fires drones at U.S. radar base in Bahrain
breaking.fact: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards fired drones at a U.S. military radar system at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain on Tuesday, the third attack on U.S. facilities in Bahrain; Bahrain said it intercepted the attack with no casualties or damage. Qatar announced new talks with Tehran as the Gulf crisis deepens.

breaking.headline: Anthropic likely to price IPO above $78, CNBC reports
breaking.fact: CNBC’s David Faber, citing sources, says Anthropic is likely to price its IPO above the $70–$78 range, with the order book closing at 4 p.m. ET today; the final price is set Wednesday and trading begins Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner put in a $5 billion order, and demand is running about seven times the 825 million shares on offer.

breaking.headline: Wall Street extends its selloff as an NSA network outage rattles traders
breaking.fact: The Dow is down about 750 points (1.5%) in Tuesday trade, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each off about 1.1%, after CNN reported an outage on a classified National Security Agency network; indexes hit their session lows on the report. Nvidia is down ahead of tonight’s earnings, its first under interim CEO Colette Kress.

breaking.headline: Senate permitting bill clears second hurdle, 70–27
breaking.fact: The Senate voted 70–27 Monday evening to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, clearing the second of three 60-vote hurdles; the final cloture test is expected early Wednesday. The bill would set deadlines for federal environmental reviews under NEPA, the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act and limit lawsuits used to block energy and infrastructure projects.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet Thursday in Shenzhen in a first-ever three-way summit
weekInBrief.body: The leaders of the U.S., China and Russia will sit down together Thursday in Shenzhen, the first three-way meeting of the world’s three largest nuclear powers, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The White House says nuclear arms reduction tops the agenda and the Iran war will also be discussed, while Russia’s war in Ukraine is excluded; officials say no agreement is expected from this first meeting, nine months after the New START treaty expired.

weekInBrief.headline: Chase software bug disrupted banking and Zelle payments at major banks
weekInBrief.body: A software bug in JPMorgan Chase’s on-premise hardware systems disrupted online banking and Zelle payments Monday, with nearly 5,000 Downdetector complaints for Chase alone and customers at Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and Truist also affected. Chase said it was a technical failure, not a cyberattack, and transactions were processing normally again by Monday evening.

weekInBrief.headline: December Fed hike now nearly fully priced as minutes land Wednesday
weekInBrief.body: Markets are pricing a near-certain December rate hike, and the Federal Reserve releases the minutes of its Oct. 27–28 meeting Wednesday afternoon. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned Monday that if the AI trade disappoints, stock prices could fall sharply and trigger an economic slowdown, adding to the pressure ahead of Nvidia’s earnings.

weekInBrief.headline: U.K. sanctions eight Israeli firms building West Bank settlements
weekInBrief.body: The U.K. government announced sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank and an activist group that blocks aid deliveries to Gaza, after Israeli settlers killed a 72-year-old Palestinian woman in Jericho overnight. The EU separately sanctioned a Gaza outlet over alleged Hamas fundraising.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: UK Maritime Trade Operations said the Panama-flagged tanker On Phoenix, first struck by an unknown projectile on Monday, was hit a second time off Oman’s coast on Tuesday, starting a fire, with its crew now unaccounted for. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claimed Tuesday that a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels and a liquefied gas carrier struck naval mines and caught fire — none of those claims has been independently verified. The USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the region, bringing the number of American carrier strike groups there to three, and Qatar announced new talks with Tehran. On oil, the blockade still holds — UANI’s Nov. 16 update says no Iranian crude tanker has evaded the blockade since July 14, and Kpler’s latest figures still put oil and product flows through the strait at about 8.3 million barrels a day in the week to Nov. 11, roughly 48% of pre-war volumes, with Iranian-origin cargoes still excluded throughout.

space.headline: Musk names the Starship booster fix: Raptor V3.2 and an earlier engine cutoff
space.body: Elon Musk said Booster 22 was “slightly low on fuel” because its engines underperformed, after SpaceX’s account of the aborted catch shifted from a guidance fault to a low-fuel-mass alarm that cut the boostback burn short. The fixes are the Raptor V3.2 engine and a flight-software change that shuts the engines down about one second earlier, and Musk said Flight 16 would aim to reuse both a booster and a ship.

space.headline: NASA aircraft dust points to a hidden water reservoir beyond Neptune
space.body: Twelve tiny dust grains collected from Earth’s stratosphere by high-altitude NASA aircraft carry about 100 times more radiation tracks than dust from the asteroid belt or Jupiter-family comets, and contain clays that form only when liquid water reacts with rock, a team led by NASA’s Johnson Space Center reports in Science Advances. The ancient water’s isotopic signature differs from carbonaceous meteorites, pointing to a separate reservoir in the outer solar system that stayed isolated for billions of years.

space.headline: Genetic ‘dimmer switch’ found that can boost sepsis resistance
space.body: A long noncoding RNA molecule called Gaplinc acts as a genetic dimmer switch in macrophages, the immune cells that drive runaway inflammation, UC Santa Cruz researchers report in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. In mice, the level of Gaplinc determined survival during endotoxic shock, pointing to a new strategy for treating sepsis, which kills at least 20% of adults who develop it.

space.headline: Vitamin B12 reverses Verheij syndrome defects in worms
space.body: Vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in laboratory worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays, researchers found. Similar metabolic changes were identified in human patients, raising the possibility that the common vitamin could inspire new treatments for rare genetic diseases, though it has not yet been shown to help people with the syndrome.

apod.title: Tossing Fireworks from Cloud to Cloud
apod.credit: Expedition 75 crew — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, November 17, 2026
apod.explanation: From the International Space Station, lightning looks nothing like it does from the ground: bolts are diffused by the clouds into bursting balls of light, and when a storm stretches for hundreds of miles it looks, as Sally Ride put it, like a transcontinental brigade tossing fireworks from cloud to cloud. This frame, taken over the South China Sea near Borneo on October 28, 2026, also catches the lights of Singapore on the left and clusters of blue fishing-boat lights like the Pleiades.
